newsitem.title: USA: Station trims more staff at Missouri casino.
newsitem.headline: Station trims more staff at Missouri casino.

text.p: Station Casinos Inc said Monday it has further reduced its work force at its new Kansas City casino following ongoing adjustments of its staff.

The casino, which opened Jan 16, cut 189 jobs from the payroll over the weekend. The casino now employs 2,751 people, down 19 percent from 3,400 when it opened. The company initially reduced staff by 162 on Feb 15.
The layoffs were across the board, including dealers, food and beverage workers and valets, said Joe Keenan, a spokesman for the casino.
Keenan stressed that revenues at the casino remain strong, but that casino officials were streamlining the work force.

"Following our grand opening it was apparent there was overstaffing in certain departments," David Fendrick, vice president and general manager, said in a statement. "We are now further streamlining our operations to provide a better value for our guests."
